alalal-e85828-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 3: whether faith can concern present things, given that vision voids faith.

alalal-e85828-d1e113.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's report that elsewhere Augustine says faith is of present things.

alalal-e85828-d1e127.summary: Objection: then vision would not void faith, against 1 Corinthians 13:10, which says that when the perfect comes the partial will pass away; faith is partial, being a mirror in an enigma.

alalal-e85828-d1e146.summary: Solution: Augustine there means the genus or substance of faith, vision of truth, which in this life is contracted to mirror and enigma as its constitutive difference; in heaven it becomes the vision that is the whole reward, not a vision merely spread over its object from outside but vision of what is loved and possessed.
claims: The substance of faith, vision of truth, remains in heaven, while its mode of mirror and enigma passes away.

alalal-e85828.summary: Article 3 reconciles Augustine's statement that faith is of present things with Paul's teaching that vision will do away with faith. Albert explains that Augustine refers to the genus or substance of faith, vision of truth. In this life that vision is contracted by its specific difference to a mirror and enigma. In heaven it becomes the vision that is the whole reward, a vision of what is loved and possessed, while faith's enigmatic mode passes away.
claims: The substance of faith, vision of truth, remains in heaven, while its enigmatic mode passes away.
